passages.text: Therefore, my brothers, whom I love and long for, my joy and crown, that is how you must stand firm in the Lord, my beloved.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the believers in Philippi.
Paul calls them his brothers.
Paul says he loves them.
Paul says he longs for them.
Paul calls them his joy.
Paul calls them his crown.
Paul tells them to stand firm in the Lord.
Paul calls them his beloved.
passages.original: Ὥστε ἀδελφοί μου ἀγαπητοὶ καὶ ἐπιπόθητοι χαρὰ καὶ στέφανός μου οὕτως στήκετε ἐν Κυρίῳ ἀγαπητοί

passages.text: I urge Euodia and Syntyche to agree with each other in the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the church in Philippi.
Paul addresses two women named Euodia and Syntyche.
Paul urges Euodia to agree with Syntyche in the Lord.
Paul urges Syntyche to agree with Euodia in the Lord.
Paul wants both women to have the same mind in the Lord.
Paul calls them to unity in Christ.
passages.original: Εὐοδίαν παρακαλῶ καὶ Συντύχην παρακαλῶ τὸ αὐτὸ φρονεῖν ἐν Κυρίῳ

passages.text: Yes, and I ask you, my true yokefellow, to help these women who have labored with me for the gospel, along with Clement and the rest of my fellow workers, whose names are in the Book of Life.
passages.sermon:
I speak to you, my true companion.
I ask you to help these women.
These women worked hard with me for the gospel.
Clement also worked with us.
Many other fellow workers joined us.
God has written their names in the Book of Life.
passages.original: ναὶ ἐρωτῶ καὶ σέ γνήσιε σύζυγε συλλαμβάνου αὐταῖς αἵτινες ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ συνήθλησάν μοι μετὰ καὶ Κλήμεντος καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν συνεργῶν μου ὧν τὰ ὀνόματα ἐν βίβλῳ ζωῆς

passages.text: Rejoice in the Lord always. I will say it again: Rejoice!
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the believers in Philippi.
He tells them to rejoice in the Lord at all times.
He repeats this command.
He says, "Rejoice!"
passages.original: Χαίρετε ἐν Κυρίῳ πάντοτε πάλιν ἐρῶ χαίρετε

passages.text: Let your gentleness be apparent to all. The Lord is near.
passages.sermon: Show your gentleness to everyone.\r\nLet all people see your gentle spirit.\r\nThe Lord is near.
passages.original: τὸ ἐπιεικὲς ὑμῶν γνωσθήτω πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις ὁ Κύριος ἐγγύς

passages.text: Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God.
passages.sermon:
Do not be anxious about anything.
Pray about everything.
Ask God for what you need.
Always give thanks when you pray.
Tell God your requests.
passages.original: Μηδὲν μεριμνᾶτε ἀλλ’ ἐν παντὶ τῇ προσευχῇ καὶ τῇ δεήσει μετὰ εὐχαριστίας τὰ αἰτήματα ὑμῶν γνωριζέσθω πρὸς τὸν Θεόν

passages.text: And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.
passages.sermon:
God gives peace.
God’s peace is greater than all understanding.
God’s peace will guard your hearts.
God’s peace will guard your minds.
God does this through Christ Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ ἡ εἰρήνη τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡ ὑπερέχουσα πάντα νοῦν φρουρήσει τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν καὶ τὰ νοήματα ὑμῶν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: Finally, brothers, whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is admirable—if anything is excellent or praiseworthy—think on these things.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes to the Christian brothers and sisters.
He tells them what to focus their minds on.
Think about whatever is true.
Think about whatever is honorable.
Think about whatever is right.
Think about whatever is pure.
Think about whatever is lovely.
Think about whatever is admirable.
If anything is excellent, think about it.
If anything is praiseworthy, think about it.
Let your thoughts dwell on these things.
passages.original: Τὸ λοιπόν ἀδελφοί ὅσα ἐστὶν ἀληθῆ ὅσα σεμνά ὅσα δίκαια ὅσα ἁγνά ὅσα προσφιλῆ ὅσα εὔφημα εἴ τις ἀρετὴ καὶ εἴ τις ἔπαινος ταῦτα λογίζεσθε

passages.text: Whatever you have learned or received or heard from me, or seen in me, put it into practice. And the God of peace will be with you.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer of this letter.
Paul follows Jesus Christ.
Paul teaches the Philippian believers.
You have learned things from Paul.
You have received things from Paul.
You have heard things from Paul.
You have seen things in Paul.
Do these things.
The God of peace will be with you.
passages.original: ἃ καὶ ἐμάθετε καὶ παρελάβετε καὶ ἠκούσατε καὶ εἴδετε ἐν ἐμοί ταῦτα πράσσετε καὶ ὁ Θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης ἔσται μεθ’ ὑμῶν

passages.text: Now I rejoice greatly in the Lord that at last you have revived your concern for me. You were indeed concerned, but you had no opportunity to show it.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer of this letter.
\r\nPaul speaks to the believers.
\r\nPaul feels great joy in the Lord.
\r\nPaul rejoices because the believers have renewed their concern for him.
\r\nThe believers cared about Paul before.
\r\nThey did not have a chance to show their care before.
\r\nNow they have shown their concern for Paul.
passages.original: Ἐχάρην δὲ ἐν Κυρίῳ μεγάλως ὅτι ἤδη ποτὲ ἀνεθάλετε τὸ ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ φρονεῖν ἐφ’ ᾧ καὶ ἐφρονεῖτε ἠκαιρεῖσθε δέ

passages.text: I am not saying this out of need, for I have learned to be content regardless of my circumstances.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the speaker.
\r\nPaul does not speak because he is in need.
\r\nPaul has learned to be content.
\r\nPaul is content in every situation.
passages.original: οὐχ ὅτι καθ’ ὑστέρησιν λέγω ἐγὼ γὰρ ἔμαθον ἐν οἷς εἰμι αὐτάρκης εἶναι

passages.text: I know how to live humbly, and I know how to abound. I am accustomed to any and every situation—to being filled and being hungry, to having plenty and having need.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul is a Christian apostle.
Paul knows how to live humbly.
Paul knows how to live with abundance.
Paul has learned to face every situation.
Paul has learned to be full.
Paul has learned to be hungry.
Paul has learned to have plenty.
Paul has learned to be in need.
passages.original: οἶδα καὶ ταπεινοῦσθαι οἶδα καὶ περισσεύειν ἐν παντὶ καὶ ἐν πᾶσιν μεμύημαι καὶ χορτάζεσθαι καὶ πεινᾶν καὶ περισσεύειν καὶ ὑστερεῖσθαι

passages.text: I can do all things through Christ who gives me strength.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul is a Christian apostle.
Christ gives Paul strength.
Paul can do all things through Christ.
Christ empowers Paul.
passages.original: πάντα ἰσχύω ἐν τῷ ἐνδυναμοῦντί με

passages.text: Nevertheless, you have done well to share in my affliction.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the Philippians.
\r\nPaul is thankful.
\r\nPaul says, “You have done well.”
\r\nYou shared with me in my trouble.
\r\nYou helped me when I suffered.
passages.original: Πλὴν καλῶς ἐποιήσατε συνκοινωνήσαντές μου τῇ θλίψει

passages.text: And as you Philippians know, in the early days of the gospel, when I left Macedonia, no church but you partnered with me in the matter of giving and receiving.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the Philippians.
Paul spoke to the Christians in Philippi.
Paul reminded them of something they already knew.
Paul said, "You Philippians know what happened in the beginning of the gospel."
Paul said, "When I left Macedonia, no other church partnered with me."
Paul said, "You were the only church that shared with me."
Paul said, "You shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving."
passages.original: οἴδατε δὲ καὶ ὑμεῖς Φιλιππήσιοι ὅτι ἐν ἀρχῇ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ὅτε ἐξῆλθον ἀπὸ Μακεδονίας οὐδεμία μοι ἐκκλησία ἐκοινώνησεν εἰς λόγον δόσεως καὶ λήμψεως εἰ μὴ ὑμεῖς μόνοι

passages.text: For even while I was in Thessalonica, you provided for my needs again and again.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul is speaking to the Philippians.
Paul was in Thessalonica.
You Philippians sent help to Paul.
You sent help more than once.
You provided for Paul's needs again and again.
passages.original: ὅτι καὶ ἐν Θεσσαλονίκῃ καὶ ἅπαξ καὶ δὶς εἰς τὴν χρείαν μοι ἐπέμψατε

passages.text: Not that I am seeking a gift, but I am looking for the fruit that may be credited to your account.
passages.sermon: I am not seeking a gift for myself.\r\nI am looking for fruit that will benefit you.\r\nI want to see results that will be credited to your account.
passages.original: Οὐχ ὅτι ἐπιζητῶ τὸ δόμα ἀλλὰ ἐπιζητῶ τὸν καρπὸν τὸν πλεονάζοντα εἰς λόγον ὑμῶν

passages.text: I have all I need and more, now that I have received your gifts from Epaphroditus. They are a fragrant offering, an acceptable sacrifice, well-pleasing to God.
passages.sermon:
Paul is writing to the Philippians.
\r\nPaul has received their gifts.
\r\nEpaphroditus brought these gifts from the Philippians.
\r\nPaul now has everything he needs.
\r\nPaul has more than enough.
\r\nThese gifts are a fragrant offering.
\r\nThese gifts are an acceptable sacrifice.
\r\nThese gifts please God.
passages.original: ἀπέχω δὲ πάντα καὶ περισσεύω πεπλήρωμαι δεξάμενος παρὰ Ἐπαφροδίτου τὰ παρ’ ὑμῶν ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας θυσίαν δεκτήν εὐάρεστον τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: And my God will supply all your needs according to His glorious riches in Christ Jesus.
passages.sermon:
God is my God.
God will give you everything you need.
God has great riches.
God gives from His riches.
God gives in glory.
God gives through Christ Jesus.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Θεός μου πληρώσει πᾶσαν χρείαν ὑμῶν κατὰ τὸ πλοῦτος αὐτοῦ ἐν δόξῃ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: To our God and Father be glory forever and ever. Amen.
passages.sermon:
God is our Father.
God deserves glory.
God deserves glory forever.
God deserves glory for all ages.
Amen.
passages.original: τῷ δὲ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρὶ ἡμῶν ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων ἀμήν

passages.text: Greet all the saints in Christ Jesus. The brothers who are with me send you greetings.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this letter.
Paul is a servant of Jesus Christ.
Paul speaks to the church in Philippi.
Paul says, "Greet all the saints in Christ Jesus."
The saints are believers who belong to Jesus Christ.
The brothers who are with Paul send their greetings to the church.
These brothers are fellow believers with Paul.
passages.original: Ἀσπάσασθε πάντα ἅγιον ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ Ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς οἱ σὺν ἐμοὶ ἀδελφοί

passages.text: All the saints send you greetings, especially those from the household of Caesar.
passages.sermon:
All the saints send you greetings.
The saints include believers in Christ Jesus.
The saints from the household of Caesar especially send you greetings.
The household of Caesar includes people who serve or belong to Caesar’s family.
passages.original: Ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς πάντες οἱ ἅγιοι μάλιστα δὲ οἱ ἐκ τῆς Καίσαρος οἰκίας

passages.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
passages.sermon: The Lord Jesus Christ gives grace.\r\nThis grace comes from Jesus Christ.\r\nMay this grace be with your spirit.
passages.original: Ἡ χάρις τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μετὰ τοῦ πνεύματος ὑμῶν
